subject: Post-demo: Atlas AI load test coordination & k6 handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Atlas AI load test coordination & k6 handoff

Hi Samir — great call earlier, thanks for walking through the integration and the SLOs. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the customer-led load run:  

Summary of performance targets you listed:
- Generation p95 target: <= 350 ms for 1k-token responses (single-stream)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s across the cluster for short-form prompts
- Streaming behavior: chunked events every ~150ms, clients expect progressive tokens with low tail latency
- Concurrency: support for 40 concurrent streaming sessions (client-side websocket) during peak window

What we need from Atlas to start the runbook prep:
1) A copy of your k6/Locust scripts (or link) and a simple traffic matrix (payload sizes, arrival distribution).
2) IP allowlist for our test agents (we'll provide IPs; confirm any corporate firewall constraints).
3) Test account(s) and an API key scoped to a non-prod tenant (read/write telemetry enabled).
4) Preferred test window — we proposed Jul 10 02:00–06:00 UTC; understood you may prefer a different slot.

Attachments: sample_k6_script.js (k6 starter), redwood-runbook.pdf (short checklist), locustfile.py (example).

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Jordan/Marissa: we prepare isolated test pool and prewarm model variants (by Jun 30).
- Atlas: share scripts + allowlist by Jul 3.
- Vivek: engineering to confirm IPs and any service-account setup (ETA Jul 2).
- Run: customer-led load test during mutually-agreed window; Redwood will provide live telemetry and a post-mortem.

Samir — can you confirm the preferred window and point person for scripts/procurement? If you send the k6 repo link + a sample scenario, Vivek will triage compatibility and we’ll generate an allowlist and temporary creds.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Thanks Jordan — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and updates from our side:
- We can target p95 <= 350ms for 1k tokens as a gate for the demo; if you have model-variant recommendations (quantized vs fp16) send them and we'll prioritize.
- Throughput: prefer to validate 200 req/s for short prompts (100–300 tokens). For longer generation (>800 tokens) we'll test at lower sustained rates (20–30 req/s).
- Streaming: we rely on chunked events; please confirm Redwood's recommended max chunk size and gap tolerance.
- Concurrency: our main app runs up to 50 simultaneous client sockets; for the test we can scale to 40 as you proposed.

Preferred test window: Jul 11, 2028 01:00–04:00 UTC (overnight for our US+EU teams).
Point people:
- Scripts & telemetry: me (samir@atlas-ai.com) and Rachna Patel (rachna.patel@atlas-ai.com).
- Procurement: procurement@atlas-ai.com for any AUP/temporary account paperwork.

Repo: https://github.com/atlas-ai/load-tests/tree/main/k6 (contains k6 scenarios and a small fixture of sample payloads).
I attached the main k6 scenario (we'll drop the full fleet scripts there).

Samir
Head of Platform
Atlas AI

Pre-run checklist (engineering):
- Create temporary test tenant + scoped API key (TTL 48h). I will create credentials once Atlas confirms the account email address and intended user.
- Reserve a dedicated pool: we will carve a 4-GPU pool (A100ish profile) for the window to keep tail predictable; Marissa please approve capacity commit.
- IPs for load generators (we can run from our public agents or accept your externally-run k6/locust). If Atlas runs agents, send the egress IPs you will use. Otherwise we will provide our agent IP list below.

Our agent IPs (please allowlist):
- 34.210.78.121
- 34.210.78.122
- 35.173.12.44
- 34.210.78.129

Compatibility notes:
- k6: we support the HTTP streaming callback via chunked responses; use simple polling for event boundaries when validating token-by-token behavior.
- Locust: be wary of websocket concurrency limits; use the provided locustfile.py sample and set swarming to ramp over 15 minutes.

I will prepare the runbook and upload a pre-run telemetry dashboard link; need Atlas repo + a short traffic matrix (payload sizes, % of long prompts) by Jul 3 to finalize capacity.
